top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, independently reproduced achievement with a distinct conceptual step beyond the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes: neutral-atom magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift for many atoms and opened the 10^-18 regime. The Katori-Ye allocation covers the concept with first demonstration and the record-accuracy realisation; the omissions of Lemonde, Ludlow and others are real but defensible if the citation is kept to the lattice clock. Moire graphene (P002) is the more promising but less mature case, since the pairing mechanism is unsettled, so I rank it second ahead of no award.
recusal_note: No conflict apparent from profile for P001 or P002. My Chalmers/WACQT ties to circuit QED (B017) are not engaged by any proposal on this slate; I have no documented link to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer.
